title.en: Volume 364 Biographies 151: Ruan Yuan, Wang Tingzhen, Tang Jinzhao
title.raw: 卷364 列傳一百五十一 阮元 汪廷珍 汤金钊

sentences.zh: 列傳一百五十一

translations.literal: Biographies 151
translations.idiomatic: Biography 151

sentences.zh: 阮元汪廷珍湯金釗

translations.literal: Ruan Yuan, Wang Tingzhen, Tang Jinzhao
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan, Wang Tingzhen, and Tang Jinzhao

sentences.zh: 阮元，字伯元，江蘇儀徵人。

translations.literal: Ruan Yuan, styled Boyuan, was a native of Yizheng in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yuan, courtesy name Boyuan, came from Yizheng in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 祖玉堂，官湖南參將，從征苗，活降苗數千人，有陰德。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu Tang served as deputy commander in Hunan; campaigning against the Miao, he spared the lives of several thousand surrendered Miao — a hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Tang had been a Hunan deputy commander; on campaigns against the Miao he had spared several thousand who surrendered, accumulating hidden merit.

sentences.zh: 元，乾隆五十四年進士，選庶吉士，散館第一，授編修。

translations.literal: Yuan passed the jinshi examination in the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, ranked first upon leaving the academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, placed first when leaving the academy, and received appointment as compiler.

sentences.zh: 逾年大考，高宗親擢第一，超擢少詹事。

translations.literal: The next year in the great examination the Gaozong Emperor personally ranked him first and promoted him in exceptional fashion to junior vice-president of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the palace examination, the Gaozong Emperor personally placed him first and exceptionally promoted him to junior vice-president of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 召對，上喜曰：「不意朕八旬外復得一人！

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, the emperor said with pleasure: "I did not expect that beyond my eightieth year I should gain another such man!
translations.idiomatic: When summoned for audience, the emperor said with delight, "I never thought that after my eightieth year I should gain another man like this!

sentences.zh: 」直南書房、懋勤殿，遷詹事。

translations.literal: " He served in the Southern Study and the Maqin Hall, and was transferred to grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: " He was assigned to the Southern Study and Maqin Hall, and was promoted to grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，督山東學政，任滿，調浙江。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he supervised education in Shandong; when his term ended he was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 58 he served as educational commissioner of Shandong; when his term ended he was moved to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、禮部、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of vice-minister of War, of Rites, and of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as vice-minister of War, Rites, and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，署浙江巡撫，尋實授。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he acted as governor of Zhejiang and soon received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he acted as Zhejiang governor and soon received the substantive post.

sentences.zh: 海寇擾浙歷數年，安南夷艇最強，鳳尾、水澳、箬黃諸幫附之，沿海土匪勾結為患。

translations.literal: Sea bandits had troubled Zhejiang for several years; Annamese foreign boats were strongest, and the Fengwei, Shui'ao, Ruohuang, and other gangs attached themselves to them, while coastal bandits colluded to make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates had harassed Zhejiang for years; Annamese junks were the strongest, with the Fengwei, Shui'ao, Ruohuang, and other gangs in their train, while coastal bandits colluded to spread the disorder.

sentences.zh: 元徵集群議為弭盜之策，造船砲，練陸師，杜接濟。

translations.literal: Yuan convened a council to devise measures to suppress piracy: building ships and cannon, drilling land forces, and cutting off supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan gathered officials to plan suppression of piracy—building warships and guns, training land troops, and blocking resupply.

sentences.zh: 五年春，令黃岩鎮總兵岳璽擊箬黃幫，滅之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he ordered Yue Xi, commanding general at Huangyan, to attack the Ruohuang gang and destroy it.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 5 he ordered Huangyan commander Yue Xi to strike the Ruohuang gang and annihilate it.

sentences.zh: 夏，寇大至，元赴台州督剿，請以定海鎮總兵李長庚總統三鎮水師，並調粵、閩兵會剿。

translations.literal: In summer the bandits came in force; Yuan went to Taizhou to supervise suppression, requested that Li Changgeng, commanding general at Dinghai, take overall command of the three naval commands, and also called in troops from Guangdong and Fujian for joint operations.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the raiders came in strength; Yuan went to Taizhou to direct the campaign, asked that Dinghai commander Li Changgeng command all three fleets, and mobilized Guangdong and Fujian forces for a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 六月，夷艇糾鳳尾、水澳等賊共百餘艘，屯松門山下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month foreign boats mustered Fengwei, Shui'ao, and other bandits in more than a hundred vessels and encamped below Songmen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the foreign junks gathered Fengwei, Shui'ao, and other pirates in more than a hundred vessels and anchored below Songmen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遣諜間水澳賊先退，會颶風大作，盜艇覆溺無算，餘眾登山，檄陸師搜捕，擒八百餘人。

translations.literal: He sent spies to sow discord so the Shui'ao bandits withdrew first; a great typhoon then arose, and countless pirate boats capsized and were drowned; the remainder went ashore, and he ordered land forces to search and capture more than eight hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He used agents to set the Shui'ao pirates retreating first; a typhoon then struck, drowning countless pirate craft; the survivors fled ashore, and he ordered land forces to hunt them down, capturing more than eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 安南四總兵溺斃者三，黃岩知縣孫鳳鳴獲其一，曰倫貴利，磔之。

translations.literal: Of four Annamese commanding generals three drowned; Sun Fengming, magistrate of Huangyan, captured one named Lun Guili and had him dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Three of four Annamese commanders drowned; Huangyan magistrate Sun Fengming seized one named Lun Guili and had him torn apart.

sentences.zh: 九月，總兵岳璽、胡振聲會擊水澳幫，擒殲殆盡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month commanders Yue Xi and Hu Zhensheng jointly attacked the Shui'ao gang and captured or killed nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month commanders Yue Xi and Hu Zhensheng jointly attacked the Shui'ao gang and nearly wiped it out.

sentences.zh: 土匪亦次第殲撫。

translations.literal: Land bandits were also successively exterminated or pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Land bandits were likewise suppressed or pacified in turn.

sentences.zh: 浙洋漸清，而餘盜為蔡牽所並，閩師不能制，勢益熾，复時犯浙。

translations.literal: The Zhejiang seas gradually grew calm, but remaining bandits were absorbed by Cai Qian; Fujian forces could not control them, their power grew fiercer, and they again raided Zhejiang from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang waters grew calmer, but remnants were absorbed by Cai Qian; Fujian troops could not contain him, his power swelled, and he again raided Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 李長庚巳擢提督，元集貲與造霆船成，配巨砲，數破牽於海上。

translations.literal: Li Changgeng had already been promoted to provincial commander-in-chief; Yuan raised funds and built thunder ships fitted with great cannon, repeatedly defeating Qian at sea.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changgeng had been promoted to provincial commander; Yuan raised funds to build "thunder" warships with heavy guns and repeatedly defeated Qian at sea.

sentences.zh: 八年，奏建昭忠祠，以歷年捕海盜傷亡將士從祀。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized to build the Zhaozhong Shrine to enshrine officers and men killed fighting pirates over the years.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he memorialized to build the Zhaozhong Shrine for officers and men killed in years of anti-pirate fighting.

sentences.zh: 盜首黃葵集舟數十，號新興幫，令總兵岳璽、張成等追剿，逾年乃平之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Huang Kui gathered several dozen boats under the name Xinxing gang; Yuan ordered commanders Yue Xi and Zhang Cheng to pursue them, and only after more than a year were they pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit leader Huang Kui gathered dozens of vessels as the Xinxing gang; Yuan ordered commanders Yue Xi and Zhang Cheng to pursue them, and peace came only after more than a year.

sentences.zh: 偕總督玉德奏請以李長庚總督兩省水師，數逐蔡牽幾獲，而玉德遇事仍掣肘。

translations.literal: Together with Governor Yu De he memorialized that Li Changgeng be made overall commander of the two provinces' naval forces; he several times nearly captured Cai Qian, but Yu De still hampered him at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor Yu De he asked that Li Changgeng command both provinces' fleets; Li several times nearly took Cai Qian, but Yu De still obstructed him.

sentences.zh: 十年，元丁父憂去職，長庚益無助，復與總督阿林保不協，久無成功，遂戰歿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Yuan left office on mourning for his father; Changgeng lacked support all the more, again fell out with Governor Alinbao, achieved nothing for a long time, and finally died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 Yuan left on mourning for his father; Changgeng lacked backing, quarreled again with Governor Alinbao, made no headway for long, and finally fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔起元署福建巡撫，以病辭。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict recalled Yuan to act as Fujian governor; he declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 an edict recalled him to act as Fujian governor; he declined because of illness.

sentences.zh: 十二年，服闋，署戶部侍郎，赴河南按事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Revenue and went to Henan on an inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Revenue and went to Henan on an investigative mission.

sentences.zh: 授兵部侍郎，復命為浙江巡撫，暫署河南巡撫。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice-minister of War, again ordered to be Zhejiang governor, and temporarily acted as Henan governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice-minister of War, again ordered to Zhejiang as governor, and temporarily acted as Henan governor.

sentences.zh: 十三年，乃至浙，詔責其防海殄寇。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he finally reached Zhejiang; an edict rebuked him to defend the coast and exterminate the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he finally reached Zhejiang; an edict rebuked him to guard the coast and destroy the pirates.

sentences.zh: 秋，蔡牽、硃濆合犯定海，親駐寧波督三鎮擊走之，牽复遁閩洋。

translations.literal: In autumn Cai Qian and Zhu Fen jointly attacked Dinghai; he personally stationed at Ningbo to direct the three commands in driving them off, and Qian again fled to Fujian waters.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Cai Qian and Zhu Fen jointly attacked Dinghai; he personally stationed at Ningbo to direct the three commands in driving them off, and Qian fled again to Fujian waters.

sentences.zh: 時用長庚部將王得祿、邱良功為兩省提督，協力勦賊，元議海戰分兵隔賊船之策，專攻蔡牽。

translations.literal: At that time Li Changgeng's former subordinates Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong were made provincial commanders of the two provinces; they cooperated in suppressing bandits; Yuan proposed the strategy of dividing forces at sea to interpose between enemy ships, concentrating on Cai Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Delu and Qiu Lianggong, former subordinates of Changgeng, were made commanders of the two provinces and cooperated against the pirates; Yuan urged dividing forces at sea to cut off enemy ships and focus on Cai Qian.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，合擊​​於漁山外洋，竟殄牽，詳得祿等傳。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year they joined battle off Yushan in the outer seas and finally destroyed Qian; details are in the biographies of Delu and others.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of year 14 they united in battle off Yushan in the open sea and finally destroyed Qian; details appear in the biographies of Delu and others.

sentences.zh: 元兩治浙，多惠政，平寇功尤著雲。

translations.literal: Yuan governed Zhejiang twice, enacted many benevolent policies, and his merit in pacifying bandits was especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan governed Zhejiang twice with many benevolent measures, and his success in pacifying pirates was especially notable.

sentences.zh: 方督師寧波時，奏請學政劉鳳誥代辦鄉試監臨，有聯號弊，為言官論劾，遣使鞫實，詔斥徇庇，褫職，予編修，在文穎館行走。

translations.literal: While directing troops at Ningbo he memorialized that educational commissioner Liu Fenggao supervise the provincial examination in his stead; linked examination numbers were discovered; censors impeached him; an envoy investigated and confirmed the facts; an edict rebuked him for favoritism, stripped his post, and gave him compiler rank with duty in the Wenyin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: While commanding at Ningbo he asked educational commissioner Liu Fenggao to supervise the provincial exams in his place; linked examination numbers were exposed; censors impeached him; an investigator confirmed it; an edict rebuked his favoritism, stripped his rank, and gave him compiler duty in the Wenyin Hall.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 命赴山西、河南按事，遷工部侍郎，出為漕運總督。

translations.literal: Ordered to Henan and Shanxi on inspection, he was transferred to vice-minister of Works and then sent out as director-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to inspect Shanxi and Henan, he was moved to vice-minister of Works and then appointed director-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he was transferred to governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 以捕治逆匪胡秉耀，加太子少保，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For capturing and punishing the rebel Hu Bingyao he was given the rank of junior guardian of the heir apparent and bestowed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing the rebel Hu Bingyao he was made junior guardian of the heir apparent and granted peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，調河南，擢湖廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to Henan and promoted to governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he was transferred to Henan and promoted to governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 修武昌江堤，建江陵范家堤、沔陽龍王廟石閘。

translations.literal: He repaired the Wuchang river embankment and built the Fan family embankment at Jiangling and the stone sluice at the Dragon King Temple in Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the Wuchang river dike and built the Fan family dike at Jiangling and the stone sluice at the Dragon King Temple in Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，調兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to governor-general of Liangguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he was transferred to governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 先一年，英吉利貢使入京，未成禮而回，遂漸跋扈。

translations.literal: The year before, an English tribute mission had entered the capital, left without completing the rites, and thereafter grew increasingly overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, an English tribute mission had entered the capital and returned without completing the rites, after which they grew increasingly arrogant.

sentences.zh: 元增建大黃、大虎山兩砲台，分兵駐守。

translations.literal: Yuan additionally built two batteries at Dahuangpao and Dahu Mountain and stationed troops in detachments.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan additionally built batteries at Dahuangpao and Dahu Mountain and stationed troops in detachments.

sentences.zh: 迭疏陳預防夷患，略曰：「英吉利恃強桀驁，性復貪利。

translations.literal: In repeated memorials he set forth measures to guard against foreign trouble, saying in summary: "England relies on strength and is fierce and arrogant, and by nature is also greedy for profit.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated memorials on guarding against foreign trouble he wrote in summary: "England relies on force and is fierce and overbearing, and by nature greedy for gain.

sentences.zh: 宜鎮以威，不可盡以德綏。

translations.literal: One should restrain them with awe; one cannot wholly pacify them with virtue alone.
translations.idiomatic: They should be restrained by awe; one cannot wholly win them by kindness alone.

sentences.zh: 彼之船堅砲利，技長於水短於陸。

translations.literal: Their ships are stout and their cannon sharp; they excel on water and are weak on land.
translations.idiomatic: Their ships are strong and their guns effective; they are skilled on water and weak on land.

sentences.zh: 定例外國貨船不許擅入內洋，儻違例禁，即宜隨機應變，量加懲創。

translations.literal: Regulations fix that foreign merchant vessels may not enter the inner seas without permission; if they violate the prohibition, one should respond flexibly as circumstances require and punish them in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations forbid foreign merchant ships to enter inner waters without permission; if they break the rule, one should adapt to circumstances and punish them proportionally.

sentences.zh: 各國知彼犯我禁，非我輕啟釁也。

translations.literal: Other nations will see that they violated our prohibition and that we did not lightly begin hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: Other nations will see that they broke our rules and that we did not lightly pick a quarrel.

sentences.zh: 」詔勗以德威相濟，勿孟浪，勿葸懦。

translations.literal: " An edict exhorted him to balance virtue and awe, neither to be rash nor timid.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict urged him to combine kindness and severity, neither to be rash nor timid.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，兼署粵海關監督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he also acted as superintendent of the Guangdong maritime customs.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 he also acted as superintendent of the Guangdong customs.

sentences.zh: 洋船夾帶鴉片煙，劾褫行商頂帶。

translations.literal: Foreign ships smuggled opium; he impeached and stripped the rank of the licensed merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign ships smuggled opium; he impeached the licensed merchants and stripped their rank.

sentences.zh: 二年，英吉利護貨兵船泊伶丁外洋，與民鬥，互有傷斃，嚴飭交犯，英人揚言罷市歸國，即停其貿易。

translations.literal: In the second year English convoy warships anchored off Lingding in the outer seas, fought with civilians, and both sides suffered casualties; he sternly ordered the culprits handed over; the English threatened to quit trade and return home, and he immediately suspended their trade.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 English convoy warships anchored off outer Lingding, fought with locals with casualties on both sides; he sternly demanded the culprits; the English threatened to quit trade and go home, and he at once stopped their trade.

sentences.zh: 久之拆閱多，託言兵船已歸，俟復來如命。

translations.literal: After a long time, with many letters opened, they claimed the warships had returned and would come again as ordered.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, with many dispatches examined, they claimed the warships had left and would return when ordered.

sentences.zh: 乃暫許貿易，與約船來不交犯乃停止。

translations.literal: He then temporarily permitted trade, agreeing that if ships came without handing over the culprits trade would cease.
translations.idiomatic: He then temporarily allowed trade, on condition that if ships came without surrendering the culprits trade would stop.

sentences.zh: 終元任，兵船不至。

translations.literal: Throughout Yuan's tenure the warships did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Yuan's term the warships never returned.

sentences.zh: 元在粵九年，兼署巡撫凡六次。

translations.literal: Yuan spent nine years in Guangdong and acted as governor six times in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan spent nine years in Guangdong and acted as governor six times in all.

sentences.zh: 六年，調雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was transferred to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 滇鹽久敝，歲絀課十餘萬，元劾罷蠹吏，力杜漏私；

translations.literal: Yunnan salt had long been corrupt, with annual shortfalls of more than a hundred thousand taels in tax; Yuan impeached and dismissed corrupt officials and strove to stop leakage and private trade;
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan salt had long been corrupt, with annual tax shortfalls exceeding a hundred thousand taels; Yuan impeached corrupt officials and worked to stop smuggling;

sentences.zh: 鹽井衰旺不齊，調劑抵補，逾年課有溢銷，酌撥邊用。

translations.literal: Salt wells varied in productivity; he adjusted and offset accounts, and after more than a year tax receipts exceeded quotas, and he allocated the surplus for frontier expenses.
translations.idiomatic: As well productivity varied, he adjusted accounts; after more than a year receipts exceeded quota, and he allocated the surplus to frontier needs.

sentences.zh: 騰越邊外野人時入內地劫掠，而保山等處邊夷曰枲僳，以墾山射獵為生，可用，乃募枲僳三百戶屯種山地，以御野人，即以溢課充費，歲有擴充。

translations.literal: Wild tribes beyond Tengyue sometimes raided inland, while border tribes called Xilu in Baoshan and elsewhere lived by clearing mountains and hunting and could be employed; he therefore recruited three hundred Xilu households to farm mountain land to repel the wild tribes, using the surplus tax for expenses, with yearly expansion.
translations.idiomatic: Wild tribes beyond Tengyue sometimes raided inland; border tribes called Xilu around Baoshan lived by farming and hunting and could be used; he recruited three hundred Xilu households to farm uplands against the wild tribes, funding it from surplus salt revenue, with yearly expansion.

sentences.zh: 野人畏威，漸有降附者。

translations.literal: The wild tribes feared his authority, and some gradually surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The wild tribes feared his power, and some gradually submitted.

sentences.zh: 十二年，協辦大學士，仍留總督任。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was made assistant grand secretary while retaining his post as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was made assistant grand secretary while remaining governor-general.

sentences.zh: 車里土司刀繩武與叔太康爭鬥，脅官求助，檄鎮道擊走之，另擇承襲乃安。

translations.literal: Cheli native official Dao Shengwu fought his uncle Taikang; he coerced officials to seek help; Yuan ordered regional commanders to drive them off and chose another heir, restoring peace.
translations.idiomatic: Cheli chieftain Dao Shengwu fought his uncle Taikang and pressured officials for aid; Yuan ordered commanders to drive them off and chose another successor, restoring order.

sentences.zh: 越南保樂州土官農文云內閧，嚴邊防勿使竄入，亦不越境生事，尋文云走死。

translations.literal: Nong Wenyun, native official of Baole prefecture in Vietnam, had internal strife; Yuan strictly guarded the frontier so he would not flee in, yet did not cross the border to make trouble; soon Wenyun fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: Vietnamese Baole chieftain Nong Wenyun had internal strife; Yuan guarded the border so he would not flee in but did not cross to interfere; soon Wenyun fled and died.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其鎮靜得大體。

translations.literal: An edict praised his calm grasp of the larger situation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised his calm grasp of the larger situation.

sentences.zh: 十五年，召拜體仁閣大學士，管理刑部，調兵部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned and appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Hall, directing the Ministry of Punishments, then transferred to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was summoned as grand secretary of the Tiren Hall, directing the Ministry of Punishments, then moved to War.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以老病請致仕，許之，給半俸，瀕行，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he asked to retire on account of age and illness; permission was granted, half salary was given, and on the eve of departure he was made senior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he asked to retire for age and illness; permission was granted with half pay, and on departure he was made senior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，鄉舉重逢，晉太傅，與鹿鳴宴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he again met the provincial examination anniversary, was promoted to grand tutor, and attended the deer-ming banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In year 26 he again celebrated the provincial exam anniversary, was promoted to grand tutor, and attended the deer-ming banquet.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，年八十有六，優詔賜卹，諡文達。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died at eighty-six; an edict of favor granted posthumous rites, and he was given the posthumous title Wendà.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he died at eighty-six; an edict granted favorable burial rites, with posthumous title Wendà.

sentences.zh: 入祀鄉賢祠、浙江名宦祠。

translations.literal: He was entered in the local worthies shrine and the Zhejiang shrine of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined in the local worthies hall and the Zhejiang hall of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 元博學淹通，早被知遇。

translations.literal: Yuan was broadly learned and thoroughly versed, and early won imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was erudite and versatile and early won imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 敕編石渠寶笈，校勘石經。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compile the Shiqu baoji and collate the stone classics.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the Shiqu baoji and collate the stone classics.

sentences.zh: 再入翰林，創編國史儒林、文苑傳，至為浙江巡撫，始手成之。

translations.literal: Re-entering the Hanlin, he initiated compilation of the Ruilin and Wenyuan sections of the national history; only when he became Zhejiang governor did he personally complete them.
translations.idiomatic: Re-entering the Hanlin, he began the Ruilin and Wenyuan sections of the national history; only as Zhejiang governor did he finish them himself.

sentences.zh: 集四庫未收書一百七十二種，撰提要進禦，補中秘之闕。

translations.literal: He collected 172 works not included in the Siku Library, wrote synopses, and presented them to the throne, filling gaps in the imperial collection.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered 172 works omitted from the Siku Library, wrote synopses, and presented them to the throne, filling gaps in the imperial collection.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，偕大學士硃珪典會試，一時樸學高才搜羅殆盡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing, together with Grand Secretary Zhu Gui he presided over the metropolitan examination and gathered nearly all the outstanding scholars of evidential learning of the day.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4, with Grand Secretary Zhu Gui he presided over the metropolitan exams and gathered nearly all leading evidential scholars of the day.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，由雲南入覲，特命典試，時稱異數。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang, coming from Yunnan to audience, he was specially ordered to preside over the examination — an honor then called unprecedented.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 13, coming from Yunnan to audience, he was specially ordered to preside over the exams — then called an unprecedented honor.

sentences.zh: 與大學士曹振鏞共事意不合，元歉然。

translations.literal: He did not agree in mind with Grand Secretary Cao Zhenyong when they worked together, and Yuan felt regret.
translations.idiomatic: Working with Grand Secretary Cao Zhenyong, he found their views did not align, and Yuan felt regret.

sentences.zh: 以前次得人之盛不可復繼，歷官所至，振興文教。

translations.literal: Because the excellence of his earlier selections could not be repeated, wherever he served he promoted literary and educational culture.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing such excellence could not be repeated, wherever he served he promoted literary and educational culture.

sentences.zh: 在浙江立詁經精舍，祀許慎、鄭康成，選高才肄業；

translations.literal: In Zhejiang he founded the Gujing Academy, enshrining Xu Shen and Zheng Xuan, and selected talented students to study there;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhejiang he founded the Gujing Academy, honoring Xu Shen and Zheng Xuan, and selected gifted students to study there;

sentences.zh: 在粵立學海堂亦如之，並延攬通儒：造士有家法，人才蔚起。

translations.literal: In Guangdong he founded the Xuehai Hall likewise, and also recruited eminent scholars: training students had a proper method, and talent flourished.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangdong he founded the Xuehai Hall likewise, recruited leading scholars, trained students by sound methods, and talent flourished.

sentences.zh: 撰十三經校勘記、經籍篡詁、皇清經解百八十餘種，專宗漢學，治經者奉為科律。

translations.literal: He wrote the Collation Notes on the Thirteen Classics, the Jingji cuangu, and more than 180 works of Qing commentaries on the classics, devoted to Han Learning; students of the classics took them as standard.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Collation Notes on the Thirteen Classics, the Jingji cuangu, and more than 180 Qing commentaries, devoted to Han Learning, which classicists treated as canon.

sentences.zh: 集清代天文、律算諸家作疇人傳，以章絕學。

translations.literal: He collected Qing writers on astronomy and mathematics in the Biographies of Calculators to display supreme learning.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Biographies of Calculators from Qing astronomers and mathematicians to honor supreme learning.

sentences.zh: 重修浙江通志、廣東通志，編輯山左金石志、兩浙金石志、積古齋鐘鼎款識、兩浙輶軒錄、淮海英靈集，刊當代名宿著述數十家為文選樓叢書。

translations.literal: He revised the Zhejiang and Guangdong provincial gazetteers, compiled gazetteers of Shandong and Zhejiang inscriptions, the Jigu zhai bell and vessel inscriptions, the Liang-Zhe imperial procession record, the Huaihai anthology, and published dozens of contemporary masters' works as the Wenxuan lou congshu.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the Zhejiang and Guangdong gazetteers, compiled Shandong and Zhejiang epigraphic gazetteers, Jigu zhai inscriptions, the Liang-Zhe imperial procession record, the Huaihai anthology, and published dozens of contemporary masters as the Wenxuan lou congshu.

sentences.zh: 自著曰揅經室集。

translations.literal: His own collected works are titled the Yangjing shi ji.
translations.idiomatic: His own collected works are titled the Yangjing shi ji.

sentences.zh: 他紀事、談藝諸編，並為世重。

translations.literal: His other records, art criticism, and compilations were also highly valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: His other chronicles, art criticism, and compilations were also highly prized.

sentences.zh: 身歷乾、嘉文物鼎盛之時，主持風會數十年，海內學者奉為山斗焉。

translations.literal: He lived through the Qianlong and Jiaqing age when culture flourished, presided over scholarly fashion for decades, and scholars throughout the realm revered him as a mountain peak.
translations.idiomatic: He lived through the Qianlong-Jiaqing flowering of culture, led scholarly fashion for decades, and scholars nationwide revered him as a towering figure.

sentences.zh: 汪廷珍，字瑟庵，江蘇山陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Tingzhen, styled Se'an, was a native of Shanyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingzhen, courtesy name Se'an, came from Shanyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 少孤，母程撫之成立。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his mother Cheng raised him to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised to maturity by his mother Cheng.

sentences.zh: 家中落，歲兇，饘粥或不給，不令人知。

translations.literal: The family declined; in famine years thin gruel was sometimes not enough, yet he let no one know.
translations.idiomatic: The family fell on hard times; in famine years they sometimes lacked even thin gruel, yet he let no one know.

sentences.zh: 母曰：「吾非恥貧，恥言貧，疑有求於人也。

translations.literal: His mother said: "I am not ashamed of poverty; I am ashamed of speaking of poverty, as though we had something to ask of others.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "I am not ashamed to be poor; I am ashamed to speak of poverty, as if we had something to ask of others.

sentences.zh: 」力學，困諸生十年，始舉於鄉。

translations.literal: " He studied diligently; after ten years as a licentiate he finally passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: " He studied hard; after ten years as a licentiate he finally passed the provincial exam.

sentences.zh: 成乾隆五十四年一甲二名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong he placed second in the first rank of jinshi and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he placed second in the first rank of jinshi and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: In the great examination he was promoted to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination he was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷祭酒。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 六十年，以事忤旨，降侍講。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year he offended the throne on a matter and was demoted to expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 60 he offended the throne on a matter and was demoted to expositor.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，直上書房。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he served in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 大考，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the great examination he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補原官。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he resumed his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his mother ended, he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 七年，督安徽學政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he supervised education in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he served as educational commissioner of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 任滿，复督江西學政。

translations.literal: When his term ended he again supervised education in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he again served as Jiangxi educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士、太僕寺卿、內閣學士，皆留任。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy, minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, retaining his educational post throughout.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Hanlin expositor, minister of the Imperial Stud, and grand secretary, while retaining his educational post.

sentences.zh: 廷珍學有根底，初為祭酒，以師道自居，選成均課士錄，教學者立言以義法，力戒摹擬剽竊之習。

translations.literal: Tingzhen had solid learning; when he first became chancellor of the National University he took the teacher's role upon himself, selected records of lectures at the Imperial College, taught students to write according to principles of meaning and method, and strongly warned against imitation and plagiarism.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen had deep learning; as chancellor of the National University he held himself to the teacher's role, compiled lecture records, taught students to write by sound principles of meaning and form, and strictly forbade imitation and plagiarism.

sentences.zh: 及官學政，為學約五則以訓士：曰辨塗，曰端本，曰敬業，曰裁偽，曰自立。

translations.literal: When he became educational commissioner he drew up five rules of study to instruct scholars: discern the path, rectify the root, revere the profession, cut out falsity, and stand on one's own.
translations.idiomatic: As educational commissioner he issued five rules for students: discern the right path, rectify fundamentals, honor one's studies, reject falsity, and maintain independence.

sentences.zh: 與士語，諄諄如父兄之於子弟。

translations.literal: In speaking with scholars he was earnest and kindly, like a father or elder brother with sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: In advising scholars he was earnest and kindly, like a father or elder brother with his sons.

sentences.zh: 所刻試牘，取易修辭之旨曰立誠編。

translations.literal: In published examination essays he took the Yi Zhuan's teaching on sincere expression and titled the collection the Licheng bian.
translations.idiomatic: He published examination essays under the title Licheng bian, taking the Changes' teaching on sincere expression.

sentences.zh: 士風為之一變。

translations.literal: Scholarly custom was thereby transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly manners were transformed.

sentences.zh: 萬載棚民入籍，舊分學額，後裁之，土客訐訟久不決；

translations.literal: Shed people of Wanzai had entered the registers and formerly had a separate quota of degrees; later it was cut; native and guest communities sued and disputed for a long time without resolution;
translations.idiomatic: Shed-dwellers of Wanzai had been registered and once had a separate degree quota; when it was later cut, natives and newcomers litigated for years without resolution;

sentences.zh: 廷珍請復分額，爭端乃息。

translations.literal: Tingzhen memorialized to restore the separate quota, and the dispute then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen asked to restore the separate quota, and the dispute ended.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed vice-minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he was appointed vice-minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 复直上書房，侍宣宗學。

translations.literal: He again entered the Upper Study and attended the Xuanzong Emperor in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: He again entered the Upper Study to instruct the future Xuanzong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 十八年，典浙江鄉試，留學政，任滿回京。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination, remained as educational commissioner, and when his term ended returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 he presided over the Zhejiang provincial exams, stayed on as educational commissioner, and returned to the capital when his term ended.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，署翰林院掌院學士，擢左都御史，充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he acted as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, was promoted to left censor-in-chief, and appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22 he acted as Hanlin chancellor, was promoted to left censor-in-chief, and made chief tutor of the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he was transferred to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，仁宗六旬萬壽，慶賀期內遇孝慈高皇后忌辰，部臣未援故事疏請服色，坐率忽，降侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, during celebrations for the Renzong Emperor's sixtieth birthday, the anniversary of Empress Xiaocigao's death fell within the congratulatory period; the ministry officials did not cite precedent in memorializing on dress colors; he was punished for negligence and demoted to vice-minister.
translations.idiomatic: In year 24, during the Renzong Emperor's sixtieth birthday celebrations, Empress Xiaocigao's death anniversary fell within the congratulatory period; ministry officials failed to cite precedent on mourning dress; he was punished for negligence and demoted to vice-minister.

sentences.zh: 逾年，复授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was again appointed minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was again appointed minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，典會試，教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he presided over the metropolitan examination and instructed the bachelors of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 2 he presided over the metropolitan exams and instructed Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 車駕謁陵，命留京辦事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the tombs he was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the tombs he was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣宗釋奠文廟禮成，臨幸辟雍，詔曰：「禮部尚書汪廷珍蒙皇考簡用上書房師傅，與朕朝夕講論，非法不道，使朕通經義，辨邪正，受益良多。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the Xuanzong Emperor completed the Confucian sacrifice and visited the Imperial College, an edict said: "Minister of Rites Wang Tingzhen was selected by my late father as tutor in the Upper Study; he discussed the classics with me morning and evening, would speak nothing contrary to the law, enabled me to master the classics and distinguish right from wrong, and benefited me greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, after the Confucian sacrifice and the emperor's visit to the Imperial College, an edict said: "Minister of Rites Wang Tingzhen was chosen by my late father as Upper Study tutor; he discussed the classics with me daily, spoke only what was lawful, helped me master the classics and distinguish right from wrong, and benefited me greatly.

sentences.zh: 朕親政後，畀以尚書之任，盡心厥職，於師道、臣道可謂兼備。

translations.literal: After I personally took power I entrusted him with the ministry and he devoted himself to duty; in teacher's duty and minister's duty he may be said to have fulfilled both.
translations.idiomatic: After I took the throne I gave him ministerial office and he devoted himself to duty; in both teacher's and minister's roles he fulfilled his charge.

sentences.zh: 今值臨雍，眷懷舊學，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Now, on this visit to the College, cherishing old studies, I add the rank of senior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On this visit to the College, cherishing old studies, I grant him senior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子報原，以員外郎即補用，示崇儒重道之意。

translations.literal: His son Baoyuan is appointed directly to the post of vice director of a bureau, showing the intent to honor Confucian learning and the Way.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoyuan is appointed directly as vice director of a bureau, showing honor for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 」四年，仁宗實錄成，賜子報閏主事，孫承佑舉人。

translations.literal: " In the fourth year, when the Veritable Records of Renzong were completed, his son Baoyuan was given the rank of junior director of a bureau and his grandson Chengyou was granted licentiate status.
translations.idiomatic: " In year 4, when the Veritable Records of Renzong were completed, his son Baoyuan was made junior director of a bureau and his grandson Chengyou was granted licentiate status.

sentences.zh: 南河高堰潰決阻運，上以廷珍生長淮、揚，命偕尚書文孚往勘，劾河督張文浩、總督孫玉庭，譴黜有差。

translations.literal: The Gaoyan embankment on the Southern Canal burst and blocked transport; because Tingzhen had grown up in the Huai-Yang region, the emperor ordered him together with Minister Wen Fu to inspect; they impeached canal director Zhang Wenhao and Governor Sun Yuting, who were punished in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyan embankment on the Southern Canal burst and blocked transport; as Tingzhen had grown up in the Huai-Yang region, the emperor sent him with Minister Wen Fu to inspect; they impeached canal director Zhang Wenhao and Governor Sun Yuting, who were punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 疏籌修濬事宜，交河督辦理。

translations.literal: He memorialized plans for dredging and repair and handed them to the canal director for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized dredging and repair plans for the canal director to carry out.

sentences.zh: 五年，回京，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he returned to the capital and was made assistant grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he returned to the capital and was made assistant grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，上震悼，優詔賜卹，贈太子太師，入祀賢良祠，命大阿哥賜奠，賜銀千兩治喪，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; the emperor was deeply grieved, granted favorable posthumous rites, posthumously made him grand tutor of the heir apparent, entered him in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers, ordered the eldest imperial son to offer sacrifice, granted a thousand taels of silver for the funeral, and gave the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he died; the emperor grieved deeply, granted favorable rites, posthumously made him grand tutor of the heir apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthy Ministers, ordered the eldest imperial son to offer sacrifice, granted a thousand taels for the funeral, and gave the posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 江蘇請祀鄉賢，特詔允之。

translations.literal: Jiangsu requested his enshrinement among local worthies, and a special edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu requested his enshrinement among local worthies, and a special edict approved.

sentences.zh: 廷珍風裁嚴峻，立朝無所親附。

translations.literal: Tingzhen's bearing was stern; in court he attached himself to no faction.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhen was stern in bearing and joined no faction at court.

sentences.zh: 出入內廷，寮寀見之，莫不肅然。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the inner court, colleagues who saw him were invariably awed into respect.
translations.idiomatic: In the inner court colleagues who met him were invariably awed into respect.

sentences.zh: 自言生平力戒刻薄，凡貪冒諂諛有不忍為，皆守母教。

translations.literal: He said himself that throughout life he strove against harshness; whatever greed, corruption, flattery, or sycophancy he could not bear to do, he refrained from by his mother's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He said he strove all his life against harshness; whatever greed, corruption, or flattery he could not bear to do, he avoided by his mother's teaching.

sentences.zh: 大學士阮元服其多聞淵博，勸著書，廷珍曰：「六經之奧，昔人先我言之，便何以長語相溷？

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Ruan Yuan admired his wide learning and urged him to write books; Tingzhen said: "The profundities of the Six Classics have already been spoken of by earlier men — with what long talk would I muddy them?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Ruan Yuan admired his learning and urged him to write; Tingzhen said: "The depths of the Six Classics were spoken of first by others — why should I add long talk to muddy them?

sentences.zh: 讀書所以析義，要歸於中有所主而已。

translations.literal: The purpose of reading is to analyze meaning; what matters is to have a settled conviction within.
translations.idiomatic: Reading is to analyze meaning; what matters is a settled conviction within.

sentences.zh: 」服用樸儉，或以公孫弘擬之，笑曰：「大丈夫不以曲學阿世為恥，而徒畏布被之譏乎？

translations.literal: " His dress and conduct were plain and frugal; when some compared him to Gongsun Hong he laughed and said: "Should a true man be ashamed of crooked learning and fawning on the age, yet only fear the ridicule of a cotton quilt?
translations.idiomatic: " He dressed plainly; when compared to Gongsun Hong he laughed: "Should a true man fear crooked learning and fawning on the world, yet only dread ridicule for a cotton quilt?

sentences.zh: 」後進以文謁，言不宗道，曰：「異日恐喪所守。

translations.literal: " When juniors presented literary works whose words did not honor the Way, he said: "Some day you may lose what you should uphold.
translations.idiomatic: " When juniors presented writings that did not honor the Way, he said: "Some day you may lose what you should uphold.

sentences.zh: 」屬官有例送御史者，持不可，曰：「斯人華而不實，何以立朝？

translations.literal: " A subordinate had someone customarily recommended for censor; he refused, saying: "This man is showy without substance — how can he stand at court?
translations.idiomatic: " A subordinate wished to recommend someone for censor; he refused: "This man is showy without substance — how can he serve at court?

sentences.zh: 」後皆如所言，人服其精鑑。

translations.literal: " Later events proved as he said, and people admired his keen judgment.
translations.idiomatic: " Later events proved him right, and people admired his judgment.

sentences.zh: 湯金釗，字敦甫，浙江蕭山人。

translations.literal: Tang Jinzhao, styled Dunfu, was a native of Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jinzhao, courtesy name Dunfu, came from Xiaoshan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 he became a jinshi, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入直上書房。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he entered the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 金釗端謹自持，宣宗在潛邸，甚敬禮之。

translations.literal: Jinzhao was upright and self-restrained; when the Xuanzong Emperor was still heir apparent he treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhao was upright and self-restrained; when the future Xuanzong Emperor was still heir apparent he treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 母憂服闋，擢侍講，督湖南學政。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended he was promoted to expositor and supervised education in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was promoted to expositor and served as Hunan educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，复直上書房。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he again entered the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 he again entered the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 典江南鄉試，留學政，詔勉以訓士不患無才，務培德，經學為本，才藻次之。

translations.literal: He presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, remained as educational commissioner, and an edict exhorted him to instruct scholars not to worry that talent was lacking but to cultivate virtue, take classical learning as foundation, and place literary ornament second.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Jiangnan provincial exams and stayed as educational commissioner; an edict urged him to teach scholars not to fear lack of talent but to cultivate virtue, ground students in classical learning, and rank literary ornament second.

sentences.zh: 金釗闡揚詔旨，通誡士子。

translations.literal: Jinzhao expounded the edict and widely admonished the scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhao expounded the edict and widely admonished scholars.

sentences.zh: 會匪以禍福煽惑鄉愚，金釗著福善辨，刊發曉諭。

translations.literal: Secret societies used fortune and misfortune to delude country folk; Jinzhao wrote the Fushan bian and published it to enlighten them.
translations.idiomatic: Secret societies used fortune and misfortune to delude villagers; Jinzhao wrote the Fushan bian and published it to enlighten them.

sentences.zh: 徐州俗悍，武生不馴者，繩之以法。

translations.literal: Xuzhou customs were fierce; martial licentiates who were unruly he restrained by law.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou customs were fierce; unruly martial licentiates he restrained by law.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎，任滿，仍直上書房。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice-minister of Rites; when his term ended he again served in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice-minister of Rites; when his term ended he again served in the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，調吏部，益鄉用。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor succeeded to the throne he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and was increasingly put to important use.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong succeeded he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel and increasingly entrusted with important duties.

sentences.zh: 時用尚書英和議，命各省查州縣陋規，明定限制。

translations.literal: At that time, following Minister Ying He's proposal, the throne ordered each province to investigate irregular local levies at the district and prefectural level and fix clear limits.
translations.idiomatic: Following Minister Ying He's proposal, the throne ordered each province to investigate irregular local levies and set clear limits.

sentences.zh: 金釗疏言：「陋規皆出於民，地方官未敢公然苛索者，畏上知之治其罪也。

translations.literal: Jinzhao memorialized: "Irregular levies all come from the people; local officials dare not openly extort only because they fear the throne will learn of it and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhao memorialized: "Irregular levies all come from the people; local officials dare not extort openly only because they fear punishment if the throne learns of it.

sentences.zh: 今若明定章程，即為例所應得，勢必明目張膽，求多於例外，雖有嚴旨，不能禁矣。

translations.literal: If regulations are now fixed in writing, they become what precedent allows; officials will surely demand more beyond the rule in broad daylight; even with stern edicts this cannot be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: If limits are now fixed in writing, they become what officials may take by precedent; they will openly demand more beyond the rule; even stern edicts cannot stop it.

sentences.zh: 況名目碎雜，所在不同，檢察難得真確，轉滋紛擾。

translations.literal: Moreover the items are numerous and scattered and differ from place to place; investigation can hardly be accurate and will only increase disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the items are numerous, scattered, and differ by place; investigation can hardly be accurate and will only increase disorder.

sentences.zh: 無論不當明定章程，亦不能妥立章程也。

translations.literal: Not only should regulations not be fixed in writing — sound regulations cannot be established at all.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations should not be fixed in writing — nor can sound regulations really be established.

sentences.zh: 吏治貴在得人，​​得其人，雖取於民而民愛戴之，不害其為清；

translations.literal: Good government depends on getting the right men; with the right man, even if he takes from the people they love and support him, and he is not harmed in being called clean;
translations.idiomatic: Good government depends on the right men; with the right man, even taking from the people they love him and he remains clean;

sentences.zh: 非其人，雖不取於民而民嫉仇之，何論其為清？

translations.literal: with the wrong man, even if he takes nothing from the people they hate and resent him — what talk is there of his being clean?
translations.idiomatic: with the wrong man, even taking nothing they hate him — what talk of cleanliness?

sentences.zh: 有治人無治法，惟在督撫舉措公明，而非立法所能限制。

translations.literal: There is government by men, not government by laws; it depends on governors-general and governors acting fairly, not on what legislation can restrict.
translations.idiomatic: There is government by men, not by laws; it depends on governors acting fairly, not on legislation.

sentences.zh: 」會中外大臣亦多言其不便，金釗疏入，上手批答曰：「朝有諍臣，使朕胸中黑白分明，無傷於政體，不勝欣悅！

translations.literal: " At the same time ministers at court and in the provinces also said it was impracticable; when Jinzhao's memorial arrived the emperor personally endorsed it: "The court has remonstrating ministers, so that black and white are clear in my breast without harm to government — I am exceedingly pleased!
translations.idiomatic: " Ministers at court and provinces also said it was impracticable; when Jinzhao's memorial arrived the emperor endorsed it: "The court has remonstrating ministers, so black and white are clear in my mind without harm to government — I am exceedingly pleased!

sentences.zh: 」予議敘。

translations.literal: " He was granted merit promotion.
translations.idiomatic: " He was granted merit promotion.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，兼署戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he also acted as vice-minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang 1 he also acted as vice-minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 兩江總督孫玉庭以南漕浮收不能盡去，議請八折徵收，學政姚文田、御史王家相皆奏言不可。

translations.literal: Governor-General Sun Yuting of the Two Jiangs, because surplus collection on southern tribute grain could not be wholly eliminated, proposed collecting at eighty percent; Educational Commissioner Yao Wentian and Censor Wang Jiaxiang both memorialized that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Sun Yuting of the Two Jiangs, because surplus collection on southern tribute grain could not be wholly stopped, proposed an eighty-percent levy; Educational Commissioner Yao Wentian and Censor Wang Jiaxiang both said it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 金釗既同部臣議覆，复疏爭曰：「康熙中奉永不加賦之明詔，此大清億萬年培養國脈之至計也。

translations.literal: Jinzhao had joined the ministry in drafting the reply, but again memorialized in protest: "In the Kangxi reign the clear edict was issued that the land tax would never be increased — this is the supreme plan by which the Great Qing nourishes the nation's lifeblood for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhao had joined the ministry reply but memorialized again: "In Kangxi's reign the edict declared the land tax would never increase — this is the supreme plan by which the Great Qing nourishes the nation's lifeblood for ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 前有議加耗米及公費銀者，戶部以事近加賦議駁。

translations.literal: Earlier proposals to add surcharge grain and public-fee silver were rejected by the Ministry of Revenue as tantamount to increasing the tax.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier proposals to add surcharge grain and public-fee silver were rejected by Revenue as tantamount to increasing the tax.

sentences.zh: 今准其略有浮收，不肖者益無顧忌，而浮收且多於往日，雖告以收逾八折即予嚴參，然前此逾額者何嘗不干嚴譴，卒不聞為之減少，獨於新定之額，恪遵而不敢逾，此臣之所不敢信也。

translations.literal: Now to allow some surplus collection, the unscrupulous will be all the more reckless, and surplus collection will exceed former days; though told that collection beyond eighty percent will bring severe impeachment, in the past those who exceeded quotas were often severely punished yet collection was never heard to decrease — that they will scrupulously observe the new quota and not dare exceed it is what this minister cannot believe.
translations.idiomatic: Now to allow some surplus collection, the unscrupulous will grow bolder and collection will exceed former days; though told that collection beyond eighty percent brings severe impeachment, those who exceeded quotas in the past were often punished yet collection never decreased — that they will scrupulously keep the new quota is what I cannot believe.

sentences.zh: 在督撫奏定之後，不慮控告浮收；

translations.literal: After governors-general and governors have fixed the rate, they will not fear accusations of surplus collection;
translations.idiomatic: After governors fix the rate, they will not fear accusations of surplus collection;

sentences.zh: 在州縣縱有發覺，又將巧脫其罪。

translations.literal: if district and prefectural officials are discovered, they will cleverly escape guilt.
translations.idiomatic: if district officials are caught, they will cleverly escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 是限制仍同虛設，徒為盛朝開加賦之端，臣竊惜之！

translations.literal: Limits will remain a dead letter, opening only a door to increased taxation for this glorious dynasty — your servant deeply regrets it!
translations.idiomatic: Limits will be empty, opening a door to increased taxation for this glorious dynasty — I deeply regret it!

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下江、浙督撫妥議，事乃寢。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived it was sent to the Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors-general for proper discussion, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was sent to Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors for discussion, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 尋以吏部事繁，罷直上書房。

translations.literal: Soon, because the Ministry of Personnel was busy, he left the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, as Personnel affairs were heavy, he left the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 典江南鄉試，道經銅山，見運河支渠為黃流淤塞，歲苦潦，回京奏請疏濬，如議行。

translations.literal: Presiding over the Jiangnan provincial examination, he passed through Tongshan and saw canal branches choked by Yellow River silt, with yearly flooding; returning to the capital he memorialized for dredging, and it was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Presiding over the Jiangnan provincial exams, he passed Tongshan and saw canal branches choked by Yellow River silt and yearly flooding; back in the capital he memorialized for dredging, and it was done.

sentences.zh: 二年，典會試，調戶部，父憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year he presided over the metropolitan examination, was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and returned home on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he presided over the metropolitan exams, was moved to Revenue, and returned home on mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 六年，服闋，署禮、工二部及倉場侍郎，仍直上書房，授皇長子奕緯讀。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Rites and Works and of the granary stores, again served in the Upper Study, and instructed the eldest imperial son Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, when mourning ended, he acted as vice-minister of Rites and Works and of granary stores, again served in the Upper Study, and instructed the eldest imperial son Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 實授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He received substantive appointment as vice-minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He received substantive appointment as vice-minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七年，連擢左都御史、禮部尚書、上方倚畀，迭命赴山西、直隸、四川、湖北、福建鞫獄按事，四年之中，凡奉使五次。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was successively promoted to left censor-in-chief and minister of Rites; the emperor relied on him; he was repeatedly ordered to Shanxi, Zhili, Sichuan, Hubei, and Fujian to try cases and conduct investigations — five missions in four years.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was promoted in succession to left censor-in-chief and minister of Rites; the emperor relied on him and sent him five times in four years to Shanxi, Zhili, Sichuan, Hubei, and Fujian to try cases.

sentences.zh: 所至持法明慎，悉當上意。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he held the law clearly and cautiously and fully met the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he applied the law clearly and cautiously and fully met the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅，調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed chief tutor of the Upper Study and transferred to minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief tutor of the Upper Study and transferred to minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，皇長子遘疾不起，忌者因以激上怒，罷總師傅，降兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the eldest imperial son fell ill and died; enemies used this to stir the emperor's anger; Jinzhao was removed as chief tutor and demoted to vice-minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the eldest imperial son fell ill and died; enemies stirred the emperor's anger; Jinzhao was removed as chief tutor and demoted to vice-minister of War.

sentences.zh: 逾兩年，復自左都御史授工部尚書，轉吏部。

translations.literal: After more than two years he was again promoted from left censor-in-chief to minister of Works and then transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After more than two years he was again promoted from left censor-in-chief to minister of Works and then to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 連典江南、順天鄉試。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the Jiangnan and Shuntian provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He presided in succession over the Jiangnan and Shuntian provincial exams.

sentences.zh: 十六年，陝西巡撫楊名颺被劾，命偕侍郎文慶往按，暫署巡撫；

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Shaanxi Governor Yang Mingyang was impeached; Jinzhao was ordered to go with Vice Minister Wen Qing to investigate and temporarily acted as governor;
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Shaanxi Governor Yang Mingyang was impeached; Jinzhao was sent with Vice Minister Wen Qing to investigate and temporarily acted as governor;

sentences.zh: 又往四川按事，名颺復與臬司互訐，得其冒工庇屬狀，劾罷。

translations.literal: he again went to Sichuan on an investigation; Mingyang again quarreled with the provincial judge; Jinzhao obtained proof that he had falsely claimed work and shielded subordinates and impeached him, leading to dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: he went again to Sichuan; Mingyang quarreled again with the provincial judge; Jinzhao proved he had falsely claimed work and shielded subordinates and impeached him into dismissal.

sentences.zh: 會京察，以奉使公明，予議敘。

translations.literal: At the capital personnel review he was granted merit promotion for fair conduct on his missions.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital personnel review he received merit promotion for fair conduct on his missions.

sentences.zh: 又赴張家口、太原鞫獄。

translations.literal: He again went to Zhangjiakou and Taiyuan to try cases.
translations.idiomatic: He again went to Zhangjiakou and Taiyuan to try cases.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以戶部尚書協辦大學士，仍調吏部。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, as minister of Revenue he was made assistant grand secretary and again transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18, as minister of Revenue he was made assistant grand secretary and again moved to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十九年，命按事安徽、江蘇、浙江。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was ordered to conduct investigations in Anhui, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he was ordered to investigate affairs in Anhui, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 自禁煙議起，海疆久不靖。

translations.literal: From the time the opium prohibition was debated, the maritime frontier had long been unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Since the opium prohibition debate, the maritime frontier had long been unsettled.

sentences.zh: 林則徐既罷，琦善主撫，復不得要領。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu had already been dismissed; Qishan favored appeasement yet again failed to grasp essentials.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Zexu had been dismissed; Qishan favored appeasement yet again failed to grasp essentials.

sentences.zh: 金釗素不附和議，與穆彰阿等意齟《齒吾》。

translations.literal: Jinzhao had never favored the appeasement faction and was at odds with Muzhanga and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhao had never favored appeasement and was at odds with Muzhanga and others.

sentences.zh: 一日召對，上從容問廣東事可付諸何人，金釗以林則徐對，上不悅。

translations.literal: One day at audience the emperor casually asked to whom Guangdong affairs could be entrusted; Jinzhao answered Lin Zexu; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: One day at audience the emperor casually asked whom Guangdong affairs could be entrusted to; Jinzhao named Lin Zexu; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 至二十一年，事且益棘，詔予則徐四品卿銜赴浙江軍營，亦未果用之。

translations.literal: By the twenty-first year affairs grew more urgent; an edict gave Lin Zexu fourth-rank vice-minister rank and sent him to the Zhejiang army camp, yet he was still not effectively used.
translations.idiomatic: By year 21 affairs grew urgent; an edict gave Lin Zexu fourth-rank vice-minister rank and sent him to the Zhejiang army, yet he was still not effectively used.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有吏部司員陳起詩規避倉差，金釗還其呈牘禁勿遞，為所訐，坐降四級調用。

translations.literal: Before long a Personnel bureau clerk, Chen Qishi, tried to evade granary duty; Jinzhao returned his petition and forbade its submission; Chen impeached him, and he was punished by demotion four ranks and transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a Personnel clerk, Chen Qishi, tried to evade granary duty; Jinzhao returned his petition and forbade submission; Chen impeached him and he was demoted four ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 逾年，授光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 以衰老乞罷，住京養疴，許以二品頂戴致仕。

translations.literal: He asked to retire on account of age and infirmity, remained in the capital to nurse his illness, and was permitted to retire with second-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire for age and illness, stayed in the capital to nurse his health, and was permitted to retire with second-rank button.

sentences.zh: 久之，上仍眷念，二十九年，皇太后之喪，具疏上慰，賜頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: After a long time the emperor still cherished him; in the twenty-ninth year, at the empress dowager's mourning, he submitted a memorial of condolence and was granted the first-rank button.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the emperor still cherished him; in year 29, at the empress dowager's mourning, he submitted a memorial of condolence and was granted the first-rank button.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，重宴鹿鳴，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng he again attended the deer-ming banquet and was made senior guardian of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng 4 he again attended the deer-ming banquet and was made senior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒，詔以尚書例賜卹，諡文端。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; an edict granted posthumous rites according to the ministerial standard, with posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he died; an edict granted ministerial posthumous rites, with posthumous title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 金釗自為翰林，布衣脫粟，後常不改。

translations.literal: From his days as a Hanlin scholar Jinzhao wore plain cloth and ate simple grain, and afterward he seldom changed.
translations.idiomatic: From his Hanlin days Jinzhao wore plain cloth and ate simple grain, and seldom changed afterward.

sentences.zh: 當官廉察，負一時清望，雖被排擠，卒以恩禮終。

translations.literal: In office he was incorrupt and observant and bore the pure reputation of the age; though squeezed out, he ended with imperial favor and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was incorrupt and bore the age's reputation for integrity; though pushed aside, he ended with imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 子修，通政司副使。

translations.literal: His son Xiu was vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiu was vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 論曰：阮元由詞臣出膺疆寄，竟殄海寇；

translations.literal: The historian comments: Ruan Yuan, rising from a literary official to bear frontier commission, finally exterminated sea bandits;
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Ruan Yuan rose from the literary service to frontier command and at last destroyed the sea pirates;

sentences.zh: 開府粵、滇，綏邊之績，並有足稱；

translations.literal: he governed Guangdong and Yunnan, and his achievements in pacifying the borders are also worthy of praise;
translations.idiomatic: he governed Guangdong and Yunnan, and his border-pacification achievements are likewise praiseworthy;

sentences.zh: 晚登宰輔，與樞臣曹振鏞異趣，惟以文學裁成後進，世推耆碩。

translations.literal: late he ascended to chief counselor; he differed in orientation from Grand Councilor Cao Zhenyong, but only shaped later generations through literary learning — the age acclaimed him as an elder master.
translations.idiomatic: late in life he reached the chief counselors; he differed in outlook from Grand Councilor Cao Zhenyong, yet shaped the young through literary learning alone, and the age hailed him as a venerable master.

sentences.zh: 汪廷珍、湯金釗正色立朝，清節並著；

translations.literal: Wang Tingzhen and Tang Jinzhao stood with stern countenance at court, their pure integrity equally renowned;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingzhen and Tang Jinzhao stood with stern integrity at court, their spotless conduct equally renowned;

sentences.zh: 金釗雖以直言被擯，宣宗終鑑其忠誠，易名曰「端」，胥無愧焉。

translations.literal: though Jinzhao was pushed aside for outspoken counsel, the Xuanzong Emperor ultimately recognized his loyalty and gave him the posthumous character "Duan" — none of them fell short of honor.
translations.idiomatic: though Jinzhao was cast out for blunt counsel, the Xuanzong Emperor ultimately recognized his loyalty and granted the posthumous name Wenduan — none of them fell short of honor.
